title: scenario-eval: an iteration's keep rule cannot tell a change the size of run-to-run noise; compare pooled runs
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① (a skill rule that cannot answer the question it is used for) · Source: fleet (the #34996 card thread's five rounds, PR #37919)

## What happens

#34996 iterates the ask skill and keeps an iteration only when one 5-run with-skill round scores above the last kept one (haiku/medium, travel_expense, 65 ask points). Its rounds read: baseline 61; r1 58 (dropped); r2 63; r3 64; r4, the same tree as r3, 59. The same tree reads 64 and 59, so run-to-run spread is about ±3, as large as the changes being judged. Pooled, the old note answers 119/130 (91.5%) and the new 186/195 (95.4%), and the targeted miss falls from 6 in 20 turns to 4 in 30: one direction, inside the noise.

`.claude/skills/scenario-eval/SKILL.md` §3 says to decide a model or effort on 5 runs per config and to report mean and min–max. It says nothing about keeping or dropping a skill iteration, so a single 5-run round above the last one passes a change the data cannot see.

## Expected

- [ ] §3 says how an iteration is kept when the change is near the spread: compare pooled runs (for example ≥15 per side, numerator and denominator pooled), or a rule that names the spread it needs to exceed.
- [ ] An iterating card's "N consecutive rounds meet the target" is read against the same rule.

Grade: area:eval · Task · reach: every iterate-until-target eval card · evidence: the rounds above (records in the thread's project files)
Suggested-grade: p2
Size: S
